data.narrative:
Mission Barns, a Series B biotech and health company founded by Eitan Fischer and David Bowman, is evaluated against a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the same sector. The company has raised $50M+ to date.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, using the $50M total raised as a proxy base, implying a $95M valuation. Peer-median analysis examines 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private comparables: Eikon Therapeutics ($539M, Series B), New Limit ($3.1B, Series C), Chai Discovery ($3.8B, Series C), and Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B, Series C). The median across these four peers is $3.5B, with a range of $539M to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied; the sector median P/S is 6.6x across the three public tickers, but Mission Barns' revenue is not on file.

The two applicable methods triangulate to a range of $81M to $4.0B, with a median implied valuation of $1.8B. The wide dispersion reflects the significant heterogeneity within the peer set, particularly the gap between Series B and Series C comparables. Key uncertainties include Mission Barns' current revenue run-rate, capital efficiency relative to peers, and stage-specific risk profile relative to the Series C cohort anchoring the upper end of the range.
